scope_reason: other:bitfield_storage_word_aliasing (sub-word read-modify-write race invisible to the logical-object SC model; adjacent to weak_memory / access-granularity)

thread_a.role: queue check updates check_* bitfields (under check_lock)

clause.resource: q bitfield word (logical field q->check_again / q->check_blocked)

thread_b.role: queue control updates klocked/locked bitfields (under owner_lock)

clause.resource: q bitfield word (logical field q->klocked / q->locked)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([write to the shared bitfield storage word]) - each logical bitfield write compiles to a word-granularity read-modify-store that must be exclusive of any other write to the same word
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@queue_access_lock:359 = write(q->klocked = 1), which RMWs the same storage word as thread_a's q->check_again write
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: EXPECTED NOT COVERED BY THIS DESIGN: each logical field is in fact correctly serialized by its OWN lock (check_lock for check_*, owner_lock for klocked/locked); there is no missing logical-level guarantee. The race exists only because the two distinct C bitfields share one compiler-managed storage word, so the two different locks fail to serialize word-level RMWs. Our logical-object contract model treats q->check_again and q->klocked as distinct locations (same_location oracle returns false), so the emergent mismatch never fires.
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ground-truth shape is a word-granularity RMW data race on shared bitfield storage; classified out_of_scope because the conflict is sub-word and not representable in the logical-object SC model, not because data_race is an uncovered category

fix_maps_to: patch converts the four bitfields to standalone bool fields so each gets its own storage byte (no shared word) -> this is a struct-layout change, NOT a synchronization change; it has no counterpart in the serialize/order/counts guarantee algebra (no lock/ordering/refcount is added)
recall_risk_notes: Design is expected to MISS this. Failure point is the same_location/conflicts oracle: q->check_again and q->klocked are distinct named struct members, so the structural grounding sees two different objects, each properly lock-protected, and finds no conflict. Recognizing the race requires C bitfield-packing knowledge (both members alias one storage word and each write is a non-atomic word RMW) - sub-word memory-layout reasoning the logical-object/SC model does not have. The fix is also a layout change with no synchronization delta to express in the algebra.
